title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen spectrum of other infectious diarrhea in Kunming, China from 2011 to 2025
abstract: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China. As the capital of Yunnan Province, Kunming serves as an important regional hub in Southwest China and a gateway to the Greater Mekong Subregion. Its patterns of regional population mobility and local disease transmission are complex and region-specific, making Kunming an informative setting for sentinel surveillance and epidemiological investigations. This study investigated the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of OID in Kunming from 2011 to 2025. Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) was utilized to characterize long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns of OID. Continuous wavelet transform was applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001). Among 38,902 laboratory-confirmed cases, viral infections predominated (99.2%). Rotavirus remained the most prevalent pathogen (69.7%), followed by norovirus (26.7%). Both were mainly concentrated among children aged 0-4 years (89.1% and 72.0%, respectively). Spatially, OID incidence varied across counties and districts, with increasingly synchronized regional increases observed in recent years, particularly after 2024. Our findings from routinely collected surveillance data indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns. Although the observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, the findings highlight increasing epidemiological complexity and emerging control challenges. Accordingly, prevention strategies should integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition.

title_zh: 2011年至2025年中国昆明市其他传染病性腹泻的时空动态及病原谱分析
source_body_en: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is one of the most frequently reported notifiable infectious diseases in China. As the capital of Yunnan Province, Kunming serves as an important regional hub in Southwest China and a gateway to the Greater Mekong Subregion. Its patterns of regional population mobility and local disease transmission are complex and region-specific, making Kunming an informative setting for sentinel surveillance and epidemiological investigations. This study investigated the long-term epidemiological characteristics and pathogen spectrum changes of OID in Kunming from 2011 to 2025. Temporal, spatial, demographic and pathogen-related patterns were assessed using descriptive epidemiological analyses, time-series and trend analyses. Seasonal-trend decomposition using Loess (STL) was utilized to characterize long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns of OID. Continuous wavelet transform was applied to identify periodic fluctuations and temporal changes in epidemic patterns. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index was used to evaluate changes in pathogen diversity. Joinpoint regression was performed to assess long-term incidence trends across different population groups. From 2011 to 2025, Kunming reported 152,090 OID cases, with a mean annual incidence of 134.3 per 100,000 population (range: 62.7-273.2 per 100,000). Incidence increased significantly over the surveillance period (AAPC = 11.2%, 95% CI 3.5 to 19.3), showing a marked acceleration after 2023. OID cases occurred across all age groups, with those aged 0-4 years accounting for the largest proportion (67.0%, 101,899/152,090), while incidence increased across all age groups (all P < 0.001). Among 38,902 laboratory-confirmed cases, viral infections predominated (99.2%). Rotavirus remained the most prevalent pathogen (69.7%), followed by norovirus (26.7%). Both were mainly concentrated among children aged 0-4 years (89.1% and 72.0%, respectively). Spatially, OID incidence varied across counties and districts, with increasingly synchronized regional increases observed in recent years, particularly after 2024. Our findings from routinely collected surveillance data indicate that OID epidemiology in Kunming has shifted from traditional epidemic fluctuations toward broader structural changes, characterized by expanding affected populations, evolving pathogen composition, and changing spatial epidemic patterns. Although the observed changes in pathogen composition may have been influenced by testing practices, the findings highlight increasing epidemiological complexity and emerging control challenges. Accordingly, prevention strategies should integrate population diversity, spatial differences, and pathogen composition.

title: Visual Detection of Foodborne Viruses in Leafy Greens Using an AsCas12f-Split-G-Quadruplex Sensor.
abstract: Abstract Foodborne viruses are responsible for a substantial burden of disease worldwide, with fresh produce serving as the most abundant vehicle for transmission. However, rapid detection in solid produce, such as leafy greens, remains underdeveloped, as conventional methods often require labor-intensive sample preparation and specialized instrumentation. Herein, we present a colorimetric CRISPR-split-G4 biosensor for rapid viral surveillance in leafy greens that combines reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA), AsCas12f-mediated trans-cleavage, and a modular split-G-quadruplex (split-G4) reporter system. In this system, target recognition activates the trans-cleavage activity of AsCas12f, resulting in degradation of a blocker strand and subsequent assembly of a catalytically active G4-hemin DNAzyme that generates a visible signal easily detectable by the naked eye. Using norovirus as a model pathogen, the platform exhibited high analytical sensitivity and specificity, enabling reliable detection of viral particles with minimal instrumentation. To evaluate practical applicability, the assay was coupled with a simplified leaf-disk extraction workflow and successfully applied to contaminated romaine lettuce and baby spinach samples without requiring viral nucleic acid purification. The platform achieved detection limits of 1000 and 5000 viral copies per 100 mg of romaine lettuce and spinach tissue, respectively. From sample processing to visual readout, the entire assay was completed in approximately 2 h. By integrating isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based target recognition, and instrument-free signal generation into a streamlined workflow, this strategy provides a promising platform for decentralized food safety monitoring and establishes a flexible framework for the on-site detection of viral pathogens in complex food matrices.

In this system, target recognition activates the trans-cleavage activity of AsCas12f, resulting in degradation of a blocker strand and subsequent assembly of a catalytically active G4-hemin DNAzyme that generates a visible signal easily detectable by the naked eye. Using norovirus as a model pathogen, the platform exhibited high analytical sensitivity and specificity, enabling reliable detection of viral particles with minimal instrumentation. To evaluate practical applicability, the assay was coupled with a simplified leaf-disk extraction workflow and successfully applied to contaminated romaine lettuce and baby spinach samples without requiring viral nucleic acid purification. The platform achieved detection limits of 1000 and 5000 viral copies per 100 mg of romaine lettuce and spinach tissue, respectively. From sample processing to visual readout, the entire assay was completed in approximately 2 h. By integrating isothermal amplification, CRISPR-based target recognition, and instrument-free signal generation into a streamlined workflow, this strategy provides a promising platform for decentralized food safety monitoring and establishes a flexible framework for the on-site detection of viral pathogens in complex food matrices.

title: Immunotoxicity Assessment of a VLP-Based Vaccine for the Prevention of Rotavirus Infection
abstract: Objective: This study evaluated the potential immunotoxicity and safety of a novel hexavalent virus-like particle (VLP)-based rotavirus vaccine candidate by assessing the t-cell-dependent antibody response (TDAR) to keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH) in Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats. Methods: SD rats (24 males, 24 females) received three intramuscular vaccine injections at antigen doses of 30, 120, or 600 μg at 14 d intervals, followed by two KLH immunizations (on d 29 and d 35). Safety was monitored via clinical signs, body weight, food consumption, gross pathology, organ weight, and plasma KLH-specific immunoglobulin M (KLH-IgM) and immunoglobulin G (KLH-IgG) levels measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) on d 35, d 42, and d 49. Results: Repeated-dose administration of the "Gam-VLP-rota" vaccine was tolerated, causing no mortality, adverse clinical signs, gross tissue pathology, or systemic organ toxicity. Absolute body weight and food intake remained within physiological norms. Comprehensive gravimetric analysis of internal organs revealed no adverse effects on the metabolic, reproductive, or central nervous systems in either sex. One-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett’s post-hoc test demonstrated that female organ weights remained stable, whereas male rats at the 600 μg dose exhibited a localized enlargement of the thymus (p<0.05). To systematically control type I error inflation across multi-dose longitudinal body weight data, post-hoc pairwise comparisons were subjected to Benjamini–Hochberg FDR adjustments, under which somatic variations did not exceed critical thresholds (adjusted q ≥ 0.3195). However, two-way ANOVA on log-transformed datasets revealed highly significant sex ⨯ treatment interactions for KLH-IgG on d 35 (p = 0.007) and KLH-IgM on d 49 (p = 0.028). Within-sex post-hoc testing with Bonferroni correction revealed a dose-dependent humoral response in females: on d 49, all vaccine groups (30, 120, and 600 μg) significantly exceeded the vehicle control group for KLH-IgM (padj ≤ 0.0125), validated by a monotonic Jonckheere–Terpstra trend test (p = 0.00097). Conclusion: The hexavalent VLP-based vaccine was well-tolerated with no overt immunosuppression or systemic toxicity observed. However, the toxicological significance of the observed thymus enlargement and antibody fluctuations requires further investigation.

title: Comparative Screening of Molecular Techniques for Detection of Foodborne Viruses in Pasteurized Milk and Mozzarella Cheese
abstract: Milk and dairy products may be contaminated by enteric viruses along the production chain, and their high protein and fat content hinders viral concentration and molecular detection. Internationally standardized recovery protocols have been established for leafy greens, soft fruits, and bivalve mollusks, but remain unavailable for dairy matrices. Three low-cost methods were compared for pasteurized milk, namely polyethylene glycol precipitation (PEG), Tris-Glycine-Beef Extract elution (TGBE), and a modified organic flocculation (FLO) exploiting the matrix’s own casein, and three for mozzarella cheese (PEG, TGBE, and glycine buffer–chloroform extraction, GBC). Samples were spiked with murine norovirus 1 (MNV-1) and murine hepatitis virus 3 (MHV-3) as non-enveloped and enveloped surrogates, and recovery was determined by RT-qPCR. TGBE yielded the highest mean recovery in both matrices (milk: 1.5 ± 0.6% for MNV-1 and 4.3 ± 0.6% for MHV-3; cheese: 4.7 ± 3.5% and 15.1 ± 17.5%), and its superiority over PEG for MNV-1 in milk was the only difference to reach statistical significance. PEG achieved recovery comparable to that of TGBE for MNV-1 in cheese (1.1 ± 1.5%) but with greater variability, whereas GBC recovery was negligible and the protocol requires a hazardous solvent. Organic flocculation yielded lower recovery (0.28 ± 0.34% for MNV-1) but allowed for processing of one-liter volumes, a potential alternative for large-volume screening of bulk milk. TGBE therefore appears the most practical candidate for viral recovery from dairy matrices in laboratories with limited infrastructure, although a larger number of replicates and validation with naturally contaminated samples remain necessary before routine application.
